title: Lucky Penny
novel:
Ted found a [[penny|penny]] on the [[sidewalk|sidewalk]] on a Tuesday afternoon. It was [[heads-up|heads-up]], and he decided it was a [[sign|sign]]. From that moment on, [[incredible|incredible]] things started happening — he caught the subway just as the doors were closing, he found a [[vintage|vintage]] [[smoking jacket|smoking jacket]] at a [[thrift store|thrift store]], and he met a beautiful woman named [[Mary|Mary]] in line for coffee.

"This penny is [[magical|magic]]," he told the gang. "Everything is going my way."

But then things started going wrong. The [[vintage|vintage]] jacket had a [[moth|moth]] [[hole|hole]]. Mary turned out to be a [[professional|professional]] [[cuddler|cuddle]] who charged by the hour. And Ted's "lucky" job [[interview|interview]] was for a company that designed [[prison|prison]] cells.

Barney [[snatched|snatch]] the penny and [[tossed|toss]] it into a [[fountain|fountain]]. "There is no such thing as luck," he declared. "There is only [[preparation|preparation]] meeting [[opportunity|opportunity]]."

"That's actually a [[real|real]] quote," Marshall said. "Seneca, Roman [[philosopher|philosopher]]."

Barney blinked. "Then I [[reclaim|reclaim]] it as my own."

Ted went back to the [[fountain|fountain]] that night, searching for his penny. He did not find it. But he did find an old man sitting alone, who told him the story of how he had met his wife at that very [[fountain|fountain]] fifty years ago. "I didn't need luck," the man said. "I just needed to be here."

Ted walked home without his penny but with something better — a [[reminder|remind]] that the best things in life happen not because of luck, but because you show up.

penny.en: the smallest unit of money in the US and UK

sidewalk.en: a path next to a road for people to walk on

heads-up.en: (of a coin) with the main side facing up, considered lucky

sign.en: something that suggests something is true or will happen

incredible.en: extremely good or impossible to believe

vintage.en: relating to old, high-quality things from the past

thrift store.en: a shop that sells used items at low prices

moth.en: a small flying insect whose larvae eat clothes

hole.en: an empty space in the surface of something

professional.en: relating to work that requires special training

cuddler.en: a person paid to hug and hold people for comfort

interview.en: a meeting where someone asks you questions to see if you can get a job

prison.en: a building where criminals are locked up

snatch.en: to take something away from someone quickly

toss.en: to throw something carelessly or gently

fountain.en: a structure that sends water up into the air

preparation.en: the act of getting ready for something

opportunity.en: a chance to do something you want to do

real.en: not imaginary or false; actually existing

philosopher.en: a person who studies ideas about life, knowledge, and truth

reclaim.en: to say something belongs to you or is your idea

smoking jacket.en: a comfortable jacket men used to wear while smoking

reminder.en: something that helps you remember something important
